notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Yellow plates with a blue strip on the left. Neighbouring countries use white plates (or black in North Africa).

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Signs usually carry two languages, one in a script practically unique to this region and one in Arabic script.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Most roads have yellow outer edge lines with white centre lines.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Red and white striped kerbs are very common; black and white ones fairly common. Red-yellow and blue-white are rare.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Stop signs show a hand instead of a word meaning stop.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Chevrons are white on black.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Kilometre markers are white with a thick border in red, green or blue.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Both A-type and B-type guardrails are common. B-type is rare in the wider region.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Utility poles often have a painted black and white striped bottom.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Utility poles with a mesh lattice framework are very common.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: A yellow warning sign is often mounted on utility poles.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Bright, warm-coloured stone buildings with a blocky look. Orange tiled roofs are more common than in neighbours; flat roofs are just as common.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Green Mediterranean scenery in the north turning very arid in the south.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The north is more mountainous and green, with forested hills nearly everywhere and occasional wide flat valleys.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The centre is mostly flat with many cities, and highways in better condition than in the north or south.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The south is extremely dry and sandy.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The Dead Sea is recognisable by the dry, barren land around it. It is also visible from the neighbouring country across the water.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The only other large lake besides the Dead Sea is far greener and more vegetated.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Date palm plantations are often seen close to the eastern border.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Rock walls held together with cement are found in the north.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The longest road runs north to south through dry land; in the far south it has a dry mountain range on its east side and palm trees.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Only some phone area codes are regional; the guide provides a map of which ones.
